q: In which year was Ada Lovelace born?
why: She was born on 10 December 1815 in London. The year 1843 belongs to her famous notes.
Her father was the poet Lord Byron. Babbage became her collaborator later.

q: Which inventor is associated with her work on the Analytical Engine?
why: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine. Ada explained its capabilities and described a computational procedure.

q: What did the procedure described in Note G calculate?
options: The number of hats at a ball
why: Note G describes a procedure for Bernoulli numbers. The name Bernoulli.exe on our website is a modern joke.

q: From which language did Ada translate Menabrea's article?
why: The article appeared in French in 1842. The English translation with Ada's notes was published in 1843.

q: What happened to the Analytical Engine during Ada's lifetime?
options: It was sold as a laptop
why: The Analytical Engine was not completed during her lifetime. She therefore could not run her published procedure on it.

q: What possibility did Ada consider for the machine beyond calculation?
why: She considered manipulating symbols other than numbers and mentioned the possibility of working with music. That does not mean she created a music app.

q: What was the youthful Flyology project about?
why: At twelve, she was interested in flight, wings and materials. The project was not a completed working aircraft.

q: With whom did Ada study advanced mathematics by correspondence?
why: Her mathematical letters with Augustus De Morgan from 1840 to 1841 are an important source on her education.

q: How is Ada Lovelace connected to the Ada programming language?
options: The language was named in her honour
why: The language was created in the 20th century, and its first standard appeared in 1983. Ada Lovelace did not create it; it bears her name.

q: Which of these projects is entirely fictional on our website?
why: TeaScript is our fictional tea language. You will find the real Ada programming language on its own page.

q: Which statement about Ada is the most accurate?
options: She invented every computer by herself
She was a pioneer; the precise label “first” needs context
She wrote the first mobile app
She founded the first cloud in London
why: She is often called the first programmer, especially for her published procedure from 1843. Babbage also had earlier unpublished procedures; her legacy includes a broader vision of computing machines too.

q: What is a primary source for Ada’s work in 1843?
why: The original notes are a contemporary document. Modern inventions cannot replace them.

q: If B₀ = 1 and B₁ = -1/2, what is B₀ + 3 × B₁?
Which operation turns S = -1/2 into B₂ = 1/6?
why: Negating the sum and dividing by three gives 1/6.

q: What does our Bernoulli simulation show?
options: A recording of the machine in 1843
An exact copy of all Ada’s cards
why: The simulation explains the principle using a modern recurrence and notation.

q: What does an AI image of Ada with a laptop prove?
why: It is labelled fiction. A convincing appearance is not historical evidence.

why: Step dependencies are part of an algorithm. A value must exist before it can be used.
